A1.justification: Both PDFs describe VIST3A, with the same authors, method, and core experiments. The main text, equations, tables, figures, and appendices A–G are readable and support reliable matching across additions, relocation, and renumbering.

before.justification: v1 reports original text-to-3D generation, reconstruction, novel-view synthesis, and ablation results, including supplementary noise-robustness experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds a human study, 7-Scenes reconstruction results, CKA analysis, and video-generation and camera-control evaluations.

M1.justification: The least-squares stitching procedure, layer selection by MSE, stitched-decoder finetuning, three reward components, and alignment algorithm remain unchanged. The dimensionality clarification and new supporting analyses do not introduce a different method.

E1.justification: v2 adds 7-Scenes pointmap evaluation and standalone video-generation evaluation on VBench, beyond the earlier use of VBench image-quality metrics. Appendix E adds a targeted camera-instruction comparison. These extend coverage while retaining the original training datasets and principal 3D tasks.

E2.justification: Section 4.4 newly evaluates CKA as an alternative indicator to the proposed MSE stitching criterion. Table 7 adds an original-versus-finetuned video-generator comparison. The established 3D baseline sets remain unchanged; the new human study evaluates Director3D, SplatFlow, Prometheus3D, and VideoRFSplat.

E3.justification: v2 introduces a distinct human-evaluation protocol: 28 participants rank five methods on text alignment and visual quality using 14 randomly selected samples from three benchmarks. It also adds video-level VBench evaluation with the original generator's resolution matched to VIST3A. These substantially broaden evaluation design, while existing training schedules and main benchmark protocols remain unchanged.

E4.justification: The analysis substantially expands: Figure 6 compares CKA with the MSE criterion, Figure 7 adds qualitative finetuning ablations, and Appendix E tests camera instructions and preservation of video-generation capability. Figure 5 replaces the ETH3D stitching-layer analysis with 7-Scenes results. The earlier reward-component scores and latent-noise robustness analysis are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, random seeds, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests for the evaluated methods. The added participant count and average rankings describe the new study's design and outcomes, without introducing uncertainty estimation.

E6.justification: Substantial new results include human-study rankings, 7-Scenes reconstruction scores, CKA findings, and camera-control examples. New Table 4 reports VIST3A average ranks of 1.54 and 1.45. New Table 7 compares original versus finetuned video generation: total VBench score rises from 0.7716 to 0.7943, while semantic score falls from 0.7275 to 0.7143. Tables 1–3, retained reconstruction columns, and reward-ablation scores are unchanged; Figure 5 changes datasets, not same-setting performance.

T1.justification: v2 adds Equation 4, a Lipschitz-based bound relating output stitching error to representation MSE, attributed to Theorem 1 of Insulla et al. This supplies formal support absent from v1, but introduces no original proof or change to the method's existing mathematics.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same principal contributions: stitching pretrained video and reconstruction models, reward-based alignment, improved text-to-3DGS generation, and pointmap generation. The new experiments support these claims without redefining the central contribution.

C2.justification: v2 interprets MSE as more precise than CKA for selecting the best stitching layer and adds explanations linking video motion to reconstruction ghosting and multi-view-only finetuning to semantic/detail loss. It also discusses inherited camera control, video-capability preservation, and backbone-selection rationale. Appendix F's limitation concerning unordered input views is unchanged.

D1.justification: The implementation information in Appendices B and C.1–C.2 is retained, including convolution configurations, loss weights, LoRA settings, optimization schedules, preprocessing, and refinement instructions. Access links are unchanged. New Appendix C.3 explains model-selection rationale rather than supplying different implementation settings or resource access.

R1.justification: v2 adds Insulla et al. to connect stitching selection with representation-alignment theory and Shotton et al. for 7-Scenes. Appendix A condenses background discussion and removes several general diffusion references while refining the comparison with encoder-substitution work. Numerous publication-year and venue updates refer to already cited works.

P1.justification: v2 removes the acronym prefix from the title, changes the publication header, clarifies feature dimensions, condenses Appendix A, and adds acknowledgments and localized explanatory passages. The overall section structure and most existing prose remain stable.

P2.justification: The visual evidence substantially expands with human-study and VBench tables, a CKA plot, decoded-versus-rendered finetuning panels, and camera-control sequences. The reconstruction table gains a 7-Scenes column group, and Figure 5 is redrawn with different reconstruction curves and axes. Existing qualitative panels and robustness plots are retained and renumbered.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens validation through direct human judgments, better justification of the stitching criterion, and tests of retained video capabilities. These address questions that v1 mainly supported through automated scores and qualitative examples. The gains are incremental: the method and established results are unchanged, the human study covers only 14 samples, and Table 7 shows a semantic-score tradeoff despite improved video quality and total score.
